title: Is fibre the new fad? “
titleChinese: 膳食纤维热”：这只是一时的流行吗？
paragraphs: Since its discovery, food businesses have encouraged high-protein diets, according to research by the University of Oregon. Whether it's bars, shakes or even marshmallows, protein has always prevailed in conversations about health and fitness. Some people think that these kinds of diets are a fad because high-protein products appear on supermarket shelves often. However, these diets have slightly stagnated within the realm of wellness.

And that's because there's now another food group gaining popularity - fibre. Found in foods like fruits, vegetables, grains, nuts, seeds, and legumes, our enzymes can't break down fibre into nutrients to absorb like it would with other food groups. Instead, it passes through the digestive system, which helps regulate bowel movements. Multiple studies have shown that certain types of fibre can lower cholesterol, help manage blood sugar levels and improve general gut health. It can also help you feel fuller for longer as it takes more time to digest.

The World Health Organisation recommends that adults consume 25-35g of fibre a day. However, research by Tate & Lyle between the years of 2021 and 2022 shows that adults in many countries aren't even close to that benchmark. The National Institute of Health tells us that the fibre intake in women is less than men. Additionally, data from the World Health Organisation shows a trend that those living outside of cities, like villages and in the countryside, have lower fibre consumption in comparison to those who live in cities.

Studies have found that not eating enough fibre can have detrimental consequences on your health. Without it, your gut bacteria can't fight excess inflammation, provide energy, or manage your blood sugar levels or your mood. Physically, you're more likely to be constipated and to feel sluggish and tired.

So, what can you do? Well, dieticians say that you should eat five to eight portions of fruit and vegetables a day. Try throwing in a handful of cooked lentils or chickpeas into curries, soups or salads. You can also eat seeds, nuts and dried fruit as your snack between meals. It might feel fashionable to talk about fibre at the moment, but science suggests that we need it to be healthy. So, be careful to follow dieticians' advice and try to eat your fruits and veggies!
chineseParagraphs: 根据俄勒冈大学的研究，自发现以来，食品行业一直在推崇高蛋白饮食。无论是蛋白棒、奶昔还是棉花糖，蛋白质在健康和健身的讨论中总是占据主导地位。一些人认为这类饮食是一种“时尚”，因为高蛋白产品经常出现在超市货架上。然而，这些饮食在健康领域的热度略有停滞。
这是因为现在另一种食物类别正在兴起——膳食纤维。纤维存在于水果、蔬菜、谷物、坚果、种子和豆类等食物中，我们的酶无法像分解其他食物那样将纤维分解为可吸收的营养物质。相反，它会穿过消化系统，这有助于调节肠道蠕动。多项研究表明，某些类型的纤维可以降低胆固醇、帮助控制血糖水平并改善整体肠道健康。由于消化所需时间更长，它还能让你更长时间地感到饱腹。
世界卫生组织建议成年人每天摄入25-35克纤维。然而，泰莱公司在2021年至2022年间的研究显示，许多国家的成年人摄入量远未达到这一基准。美国国立卫生研究院告诉我们，女性的纤维摄入量低于男性。此外，世界卫生组织的数据显示出一个趋势：与居住在城市的人相比，居住在农村等非城市地区的人纤维摄入量较低。
研究发现，摄入纤维不足可能对你的健康产生不利影响。没有纤维，你的肠道细菌就无法抵抗过度炎症、提供能量，或管理你的血糖水平和情绪。身体上来说，你更容易便秘，感到无精打采和疲惫。
那么，你能做些什么呢？营养师建议每天吃五到八份水果和蔬菜。试着在咖喱、汤或沙拉中加入一把煮熟的扁豆或鹰嘴豆。你也可以在两餐之间吃种子、坚果和果干作为零食。目前谈论纤维可能感觉很时髦，但科学表明我们需要它来保持健康。所以，务必遵循营养师的建议，多吃水果和蔬菜！

vocabulary.definition: 占主导地位，盛行（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: prevail /prɪˈveɪl/ v. 占主导地位，盛行（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Justice will prevail in the end.
vocabulary.translation: 正义终将获胜。

vocabulary.entry: fad /fæd/ n. 时尚，一时的狂热（口语）
vocabulary.example: Low-carb diets were a fad in the 1990s.
vocabulary.translation: 低碳水饮食在20世纪90年代曾是一种时尚。

vocabulary.entry: stagnate /stæɡˈneɪt/ v. 停滞，不发展（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The economy has stagnated in recent years.
vocabulary.translation: 近年来经济一直停滞不前。

vocabulary.entry: realm /relm/ n. 领域，范围（书面语）
vocabulary.example: She is an expert in the realm of psychology.
vocabulary.translation: 她是心理学领域的专家。

vocabulary.entry: fibre /ˈfaɪbə(r)/ n. 纤维
vocabulary.example: Fruit and vegetables are a good source of dietary fibre.
vocabulary.translation: 水果和蔬菜是膳食纤维的良好来源。

vocabulary.definition: 豆科植物，豆类（专业术语）
vocabulary.entry: legume /ˈleɡjuːm/ n. 豆科植物，豆类（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Legumes such as beans and lentils are rich in protein.
vocabulary.translation: 豆子和扁豆等豆类富含蛋白质。

vocabulary.definition: 酶（生物化学专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: enzyme /ˈenzaɪm/ n. 酶（生物化学专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: The enzyme is found in the saliva of certain insects.
vocabulary.translation: 这种酶存在于某些昆虫的唾液中。

vocabulary.entry: break down /ˌbreɪk ˈdaʊn/ phr. v. 分解（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Plastic takes hundreds of years to break down.
vocabulary.translation: 塑料需要数百年才能分解。

vocabulary.entry: digestive system /daɪˈdʒestɪv ˌsɪstəm/ n. 消化系统（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: A healthy digestive system is important for overall wellbeing.
vocabulary.translation: 健康的消化系统对整体健康很重要。

vocabulary.entry: bowel movement /ˈbaʊəl ˌmuːvmənt/ n. 排便（医学术语）
vocabulary.example: Fibre helps regulate bowel movements.
vocabulary.translation: 纤维有助于调节排便。

vocabulary.definition: 胆固醇（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: cholesterol /kəˈlestərɒl/ n. 胆固醇（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: High cholesterol can lead to heart disease.
vocabulary.translation: 高胆固醇可导致心脏病。

vocabulary.entry: blood sugar level /ˈblʌd ʃʊɡə ˌlevl/ n. 血糖水平（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Diabetics need to monitor their blood sugar levels.
vocabulary.translation: 糖尿病患者需要监测血糖水平。

vocabulary.entry: gut health /ˈɡʌt helθ/ n. 肠道健康（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Probiotics can improve gut health.
vocabulary.translation: 益生菌可以改善肠道健康。

vocabulary.entry: consume /kənˈsjuːm/ v. 消费，吃/喝掉（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The average person consumes a lot of sugar in their diet.
vocabulary.translation: 普通人在饮食中摄入大量糖分。

vocabulary.entry: benchmark /ˈbentʃmɑːk/ n. 基准，参照标准（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The company's performance is used as a benchmark for others.
vocabulary.translation: 该公司的业绩被用作其他公司的基准。

vocabulary.entry: intake /ˈɪnteɪk/ n. 摄入量，吸入（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The doctor advised him to reduce his salt intake.
vocabulary.translation: 医生建议他减少盐的摄入量。

vocabulary.entry: detrimental /ˌdetrɪˈmentl/ adj. 有害的，不利的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Smoking is detrimental to your health.
vocabulary.translation: 吸烟对健康有害。

vocabulary.entry: consequence /ˈkɒnsɪkwəns/ n. 结果，后果（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The consequences of the decision could be serious.
vocabulary.translation: 这个决定的后果可能很严重。

vocabulary.entry: inflammation /ˌɪnfləˈmeɪʃn/ n. 炎症（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: Chronic inflammation is linked to many diseases.
vocabulary.translation: 慢性炎症与许多疾病有关。

vocabulary.entry: constipated /ˈkɒnstɪpeɪtɪd/ adj. 便秘的（医学术语）
vocabulary.example: Lack of fibre can make you constipated.
vocabulary.translation: 缺乏纤维会导致便秘。

vocabulary.definition: 无精打采的，迟缓的（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: sluggish /ˈslʌɡɪʃ/ adj. 无精打采的，迟缓的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: After a heavy meal, I feel sluggish.
vocabulary.translation: 吃了一顿大餐后，我感到无精打采。

vocabulary.definition: 营养师，膳食学家（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: dietician /ˌdaɪəˈtɪʃn/ n. 营养师，膳食学家（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The dietician advised her to eat more fruit and vegetables.
vocabulary.translation: 营养师建议她多吃水果和蔬菜。

vocabulary.entry: portion /ˈpɔːʃn/ n. 一份，一部分
vocabulary.example: She gave me a generous portion of cake.
vocabulary.translation: 她给了我一大块蛋糕。

vocabulary.entry: curry /ˈkʌri/ n. 咖喱，咖喱菜肴
vocabulary.example: We went for an Indian curry last night.
vocabulary.translation: 我们昨晚去吃了印度咖喱。

vocabulary.entry: lentil /ˈlentl/ n. 扁豆
vocabulary.example: Lentil soup is hearty and nutritious.
vocabulary.translation: 扁豆汤既丰盛又有营养。

vocabulary.entry: chickpea /ˈtʃɪkpiː/ n. 鹰嘴豆
vocabulary.example: Chickpeas are the main ingredient in hummus.
vocabulary.translation: 鹰嘴豆是鹰嘴豆泥的主要成分。

vocabulary.entry: snack /snæk/ n. 零食，小吃
vocabulary.example: She had a snack between meals.
vocabulary.translation: 她在两餐之间吃了一份零食。
